newsitem.title: ITALY: BA to complain to EU on Alitalia aid.
newsitem.headline: BA to complain to EU on Alitalia aid.

text.p: British Airways Plc said it will complain to the European Commission over what it regards as unfair state aid to troubled Italian flag carrier Alitalia.
BA chief executive Robert Ayling told a Milan news conference the company intended to put its protest to European Transport Commissioner Neil Kinnock.
BA "does not look kindly on state contributions to companies. We will be seeing Kinnock soon to put forward our objections," he said after a BA annual European meeting.
Ayling said aid to Alitalia, just like in France with Air France, constituted unfair competition "for those like us who do not get state subsidies."

"We have already filed a complaint with the Court of Justice in Luxembourg about the French situation, which is similar to the Italian case, and its sentence will be valid for all similar cases," Ayling said.
Alitalia's parent company, state-controlled IRI, threw the carrier a lifeline in July when it agreed to a 3.135 trillion lire recapitalisation designed to save it from collapse.
IRI has pledged to inject 1.5 trillion of fresh funds under the capital increase. The remainder is due to come from the private sector next year.
The European Commission has said it aimed to reach a decision by the end of this month on whether to clear the Alitalia rescue plan.

BA Chairman Sir Colin Marshall, referring to the company's proposed alliance with American Airlines, said if the plan was approved "there could be an increase in employment in Great Britain, particularly in Manchester and Birmingham."
UK competition authorities are currently reviewing the proposed alliance with American Airlines, part of AMR Corp, and trade and industry minister Ian Lang is expected to report next week.
Under the planned link-up, BA aims to coordinate its 244 weekly flights from Britain to 22 U.S. destinations with American's 238 flights from seven U.S. airports to 12 European destinations.
